page.title: Maintenance schedules
page.description: What runs on its own to keep this tenant's data healthy: integrity checks, directory sync and retention. Backups and their restore checks are backup jobs.

kindHints.backup: Backs up every active protected object, or only the one you choose.
kindHints.verify: Restores a sample of the latest backup to prove it can be restored. While a restore check schedule is on, every new backup is checked as well.
kindHints.scrub: Checks the stored packs for damage and repairs them from copies. Monthly or rarer runs check everything, more frequent runs a sample.
kindHints.directory: Reads users, mailboxes and OneDrives from Microsoft Entra ID, so new people are protected by the rules.
kindHints.retention: Applies the retention policies. Until a policy exists, everything is kept.

errors.load: The schedules could not be loaded

noTenant.title: No tenant selected
noTenant.description: Select a tenant to see and change its schedules.

empty.title: No maintenance schedules yet
empty.description: Nothing keeps the repository healthy on its own: integrity checks, directory sync and retention run only when someone starts them.

notices.readOnly: You can see the schedules of this tenant. Only tenant administrators can change them.

noJob.title: Backups are not set up on a schedule
noJob.description: No mail job covers all protected objects of this tenant, and no older schedule does. Without one, backups and restore checks run only when someone starts them. The recommended set creates the mail job.

notices.legacy: Listed here: {count, plural, one {# older backup or restore-check schedule} other {# older backup and restore-check schedules}}. Schedules like these keep running next to the jobs. Switch one off or delete it once a job covers the same objects.
notices.retention: Retention applies the retention policies. Until a policy exists, everything is kept.

form.description: Choose what runs, how often and for which objects.
form.dayOfMonthHint: 1 to {max}: every month has these days.
form.cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Example: 30 4 * * 1-5 runs at 04:30 from Monday to Friday.
form.intervalStartsNow: The first run starts within a minute of saving; later runs count from the previous one.
form.intervalFromLastRun: Runs count from the last run.
form.timezoneHint: Times are local times in this zone; daylight saving time is taken into account.
form.previewRefused: No runs: correct the marked field.
form.previewIncomplete: Complete the cadence to see the next runs.
form.enabledHint: Switched off, the schedule keeps its settings but does not run.

required.dayOfMonth: Enter a day of the month.

problems.cadence_missing: Choose how often the schedule runs.
problems.cadence_ambiguous: Use either an interval or a cron expression, not both.
problems.interval_not_integer: The interval must be whole minutes.
problems.interval_out_of_range: The interval must be between 15 minutes and 31 days.
problems.cron_invalid: This is not a valid cron expression.
problems.cron_never_matches: This expression never matches a date.
problems.cron_too_frequent: Runs must be at least 15 minutes apart.
problems.scope_not_supported: This kind of schedule always runs for the whole tenant.
problems.object_not_found: The protected object no longer exists.
problems.generic: The schedule cannot be saved like this.

delete.title: Delete this schedule?
delete.description: It will no longer run on its own. Runs already queued are not affected, and the settings cannot be brought back.

backup.title: Switch off automatic backups?
backup.description: While it is off, the objects it covers are backed up only when someone starts a backup by hand.

verify.title: Switch off the restore check?
verify.description: While it is off, new backups are not test-restored and recovery readiness is no longer proven.

toasts.applied: {count, plural, one {# recommended schedule added} other {# recommended schedules added}}
toasts.failed: The change could not be saved
